name: The Golden Apple
description: A gleaming apple of untarnished electrum, small enough for the palm yet impossibly heavy with portent. Inscribed faintly with the words 'Τῇ Kαλλίστῃ' (To the Fairest).
lore: Cast by Eris at the wedding of Peleus and Thetis, the apple sparked rivalry among goddesses and set the Trojan War in motion. In Pangea its mere presence sows distrust, forcing every bearer to confront the shadow of envy.
origin: Plucked from the Garden of the Hesperides at the western edge of the world and later hidden in a reliquary beneath Delphi's ruined omphalos.

name: The Book of Thoth
description: A papyrus codex bound by electrum clasps, its pages shift between visible ink and shimmering hieroglyphs that rearrange when read aloud.
lore: Legend says the ibis-headed god penned the spells inside, granting mastery over tongues of beasts, dominion of the waters, and sight into Duat. Those who read without ritual purity suffer madness as sacred ibis talons shred their mind.
origin: Entombed with an unnamed prince in a submerged crypt near Hermopolis Magna; reclaimed by Alexandrian adepts during the reign of Ptolemy Philadelphus.

name: Cintamani Stone
description: A teardrop of radiant azure that pulses like a heartbeat; when held in darkness it projects constellations of unrealised futures.
lore: Revered in Hindu and Tibetan Buddhism as the 'jewel that fell from the sky.'  It grants the pure in heart a single world-shaping boon, but burns the grasp of the selfish to ash. Rumoured fragment of a larger meteorite altar in Shambhala.
origin: Carried from the Himalayas by Nagas to Lake Manasarovar, later smuggled west along the Alum Silk Route by Nestorian monks.

name: The Cup of Jamshid
description: A flawless crystal chalice filled perpetually with liquid starlight that swirls into living panoramas of past, present, and myriad possible futures.
lore: King Jamshid consulted its surface to rule the Four Quarters.  Magi claim each use fractures another shard off destiny's mirror; overuse can shatter an era entirely.
origin: Fashioned in the Achaemenid fire-temple of Takht-e Jamshid from sand fused by a comet strike in 536 BCE.

name: The Kusanagi
description: A curved tachi whose hamon resembles wind-tossed grass; the blade hums faintly with unseen cicadas when injustice is near.
lore: Drawn by the storm-god Susanoo from the corpse of the eight-headed Orochi, the sword 'that cuts the grass' saved Prince Yamato Takeru from wildfire and became one of Japan's Three Sacred Treasures.  It severs falsehood as easily as silk.
origin: Kept within the innermost shrine at Atsuta, but a phantom echo of the blade traverses vistas where the Imperial Regalia never came to be.

name: The Philosopher's Stone
description: A rough red crystal the size of a quail's egg; when placed on metal it sweats mercurial dew that turns lead to gold and flesh to perennial youth.
lore: Said to be the densest concentration of Prima Materia distilled by Hermes Trismegistus and transmitted through Arabic *al-iksir* manuscripts.  Each transmutation brings the wielder nearer to the 'One Thing,' yet risks dissolving their identity into cosmic quintessence.
origin: First precipitated in the glass retorts of Alexandria's Serapeum, later scattered as powder in Moorish Toledo before re-coalescing in secret Athanor labs across Europe.

name: The Sword of Destiny
description: A double-edged longsword forged of star-iron, its fuller inlaid with runes that glow only when the bearer stands at a crossroads of history.
lore: Forged by druid-smiths on the Isle of Avalon under a meteor shower, the blade guides the hand of the rightful changer-of-worlds.  The sword cannot be unsheathed for selfish ends—attempts to do so turn its edge to rust.
origin: Guarded in a crystal scabbard beneath the roots of Glastonbury Tor until Arthurian upheavals scattered its fragments across timelines; in Pangea it seeks reassembly through the *Trionfi* arcana.

name: Masons' Tools
description: A triad of silvered square, compass, and setting-maul bound with indigo cord, each etched with geometric sigils that rearrange to reveal hidden angles.
lore: Said to be the very implements Hiram Abiff used to lay Solomon's Temple cornerstone.  When aligned atop a ley nexus, they trace a luminous blueprint of whatever the wielder most yearns to build—be it cathedral, civilization, or cosmic order.
origin: Passed down through clandestine guilds from Jerusalem to medieval Strasbourg; currently locked in a cedar ark aboard the Zanetti Train's freight car marked 'G'.
